This is the simulation from [The Statistical Significance Filter](../concepts/statistical-significance-filter.qmd), written in R. It runs in your browser with [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/), a version of R compiled to WebAssembly, so there is nothing to install. The first time, your browser downloads R itself, which can take a minute. Edit any line and click **Run Code** to try it with other values.

R draws different random numbers from the entry page, so the individual dots differ, but the results tell the same story.

## One study, replicated 400 times

```{webr}
set.seed(42)
theta <- 0.2   # true effect
se    <- 0.25  # standard error of each study
n_rep <- 400   # number of replications

est <- rnorm(n_rep, mean = theta, sd = se)
sig <- abs(est) > 1.96 * se          # statistically significant at the 5% level

power <- pnorm(theta / se - 1.96) + pnorm(-theta / se - 1.96)
avg_sig <- mean(abs(est[sig]))

cat("Power:", round(power, 2), "\n")
cat("Significant replications:", sum(sig), "of", n_rep, "\n")
cat("Average magnitude of the significant estimates:", round(avg_sig, 2), "\n")
cat("Exaggeration ratio:", round(avg_sig / theta, 1), "\n")
cat("Significant estimates with the wrong sign:", sum(sign(est[sig]) != sign(theta)), "\n")

plot(est, pch = ifelse(sig, 19, 1), col = ifelse(sig, "#d6604d", "grey50"),
     xlab = "Replication", ylab = "Estimated effect")
abline(h = c(-1.96, 1.96) * se, lty = 2, col = "grey50")  # significance thresholds
abline(h = theta, col = "#2166ac", lwd = 2)                # the true effect
abline(h = 0)
```

## Exaggeration grows as power falls

Gelman and Carlin's [design analysis](https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691614551642) asks how much a significant estimate overstates the truth, on average, at a given power. Here it is for a range of true effects with the standard error fixed at 0.25.

```{webr}
exaggeration <- function(theta, se, n_sims = 1e5) {
  est <- rnorm(n_sims, mean = theta, sd = se)
  sig <- abs(est) > 1.96 * se
  mean(abs(est[sig])) / theta
}

se     <- 0.25
thetas <- seq(0.05, 1, by = 0.05)
power  <- pnorm(thetas / se - 1.96) + pnorm(-thetas / se - 1.96)
ratio  <- sapply(thetas, exaggeration, se = se)

plot(power, ratio, type = "b", pch = 19, log = "y",
     xlab = "Power", ylab = "Exaggeration ratio (log scale)")
abline(h = 1, lty = 2)
round(data.frame(power, ratio)[c(1, 4, 8, 12, 20), ], 2)
```
